data.headline: Power Rankings Week 4: Undefeated Kings and a Shart Parade
data.deck: Two teams are still 4-0, one team is still winless, and 11 weeks remain to sort out the other 11 lives currently in freefall.
body: 14 teams, 7 playoff spots, 11 weeks left to figure out who's actually good and who's just rich in garbage points for. Here's where everybody sits after Week 4.
1. 50 Shades of Zay (Trip): Sits at 4-0 with 533.72 points for, the kind of record that makes bubble teams weep into their waiver claims.
2. Ha Ha Ha, Now Heres A Guy (Jackson): Also 4-0 at 527.8 points for, hoarding 1 Manager of the Week trophy like it's a participation ribbon he actually earned.

3. Chase Browns with Downs (Jeff): Rode Javonte Williams's 31.3 to a 115.9 beatdown of Matt, quietly sitting on 76.7 percent playoff odds, which sounds like a lot until you remember he has to keep doing this.
4. BedBathNBIJAN22 (John): Sitting on 533.38 points for with a 2-2 record, which means he's either the unluckiest scheduling victim in Squirtnite or just has a real problem closing.
5. Zyn-bo Squisher (Josef): Dropped 112.7 on Bearcat's face, a 39.68 margin that reads less like a win and more like an eviction notice.
6. Cook'd (Jack): Climbed a spot because Tetairoa McMillan decided to PERSONALLY torch Bibi's Ballers 69 for 45.2, and Jack just had to show up to collect the 154.78.
7. Jackson Off (Ben): Fell a spot after losing the Game of the Week by 2.84, the fantasy equivalent of getting dumped over text and finding out on the group chat.
8. First Down Syndrome (Adam): Got 509.24 points for and a 1-3 record, somehow managing to lose every close one like it's a lifestyle choice.
9. Bibi's Ballers 69 (Andrew): Owns 1 Manager of the Week award from earlier this season and also just got run for 154.78, proof past success means nothing in this league.
10. Hog tied and deep fried (Bearcat): Moved up a slot despite scoring 73.02, which tells you everything you need to know about how bad things are below him.
11. Romo911 (Aaron): Has 2 Shart Awards sitting in his trophy case and still beat Adam 118.18 to 88.72 on the back of Nico Collins's 30.8, chaos agent behavior if there ever was any.

12. Burrowed Alive (Sean): Won the single closest game of the week, 149.42 to 146.58, thanks to CeeDee Lamb's 41.3, and still sits 12th because the rest of his season has been a straight up CRIME SCENE.
13. Shough Her Gently (Matt): Those 15.2 percent playoff odds aren't a typo, they're just an honest reflection of a 370.86 points for total that wouldn't scare a bye week.
14. Victorious Secrets (Taylor): Got 36.7 out of Kyren Williams and still lost 78.86 to 124.48, the kind of stat line that makes you check if your kicker started by accident.

data.headline: The Waiver Wire Was a Ghost Town This Week
data.deck: Nobody moved. Nobody flinched. The league just sat there like it was waiting for permission.
body: Let's be honest about what happened on the wire this week in Squirtnite FFL: nothing. Zero trades, logged right there in black and white, and apparently zero waiver claims worth writing home about either. Fourteen grown men had a full week to fix something and collectively decided to just vibe.

Which is a bold strategy considering what actually went down on the field. Tayodin got run over 78.86 to 124.48 and didn't reach for the emergency lever. Matt watched Shough Her Gently fall to 87.38 and still didn't touch the roster. Bearcat got stomped 73.02 to 112.7 and apparently thought 'this is fine.' These are the bottom-feeders of this league, sitting at the kids' table with the worst records, and the waiver wire sat there untouched like a buffet nobody trusted.

Meanwhile Tetairoa McMillan dropped 45.2 points for Jack and CeeDee Lamb went for 41.3 for Sean, reminders that difference-makers exist out there for the taking. Somebody's going to find that guy. It's just apparently not going to be any of you this week.
Get off your asses before next week's slate. The standings aren't waiting.
data.signOff: See you on the wire, cowards.

data.headline: Burrowed Alive Survives By A Paper Cut
data.deck: Sean finds 149.42 points hiding in a 1-3 record and escapes Ben by the width of CeeDee Lamb's fingertips
body: This was supposed to be the week Jackson Off buried Burrowed Alive for good. Instead Sean dug himself out of his own grave with a shovel made of pure desperation and won by 2.84 points, which in fantasy terms is basically a coin flip that landed on its edge and stayed there out of spite.

CeeDee Lamb did the heavy lifting for Sean, dropping 41.3 points on a roster that came into the week 1-3 and smelling like it. Ben countered with 146.58 of his own, a totally respectable number that will haunt him anyway because respectable doesn't win you anything when the other guy finds 149.42 from somewhere.

Sean is still sitting at 1-3 with a playoff odds number so low it needs a stepladder, 8.8 percent, and this win barely moves the needle. But a win is a win, and for one week Sean gets to walk around like he didn't just scrape together a 404.44 points-for season on a prayer and a Cowboys receiver.

Ben, meanwhile, drops to 2-2 and watches his power ranking slide a spot while everyone reminds him that 146.58 points should be enough to beat literally anyone except, apparently, the exact guy he played. Next week Ben gets 50 Shades of Zay, which is its own kind of punishment. Sean gets Bibi's Ballers 69, a team currently sitting at 1-3 with a points-for of 508.6, meaning this nonsense is nowhere close to over for either of them.

data.headline: Seven Games, One Theme: Mercy Is Dead
data.deck: Blowouts, a bloodbath, and one nail biter that decided literally one thing nobody asked about.
body: Sean somehow survived Jackson Off by 2.84, winning 149.42 to 146.58 behind CeeDee Lamb's 41.3. Ben put up 146.58 and still lost, which is the fantasy equivalent of acing the test and failing the class because you forgot your name on the paper.

Trip and 50 Shades of Zay moved to 4-0 by torching Victorious Secrets 124.48 to 78.86. Taylor got 36.7 out of Kyren Williams and still lost by 45.62, which tells you everything about the rest of that roster.

Jack's Cook'd dropped 154.78 on Bibi's Ballers 69 thanks to Tetairoa McMillan going off for 45.2, the single biggest number anybody put up all week. Andrew lost by 44.02 and should probably not look directly at his lineup for a few days.
Josef and Zyn-bo Squisher handled Hog tied and deep fried 112.7 to 73.02. Bearcat's team name is now doing more work than his roster.
Jeff's Chase Browns with Downs beat Matt's Shough Her Gently 115.9 to 87.38, with Javonte Williams putting up 31.3. Matt is 1-3 and the vibes are not improving.
Aaron's Romo911 topped First Down Syndrome 118.18 to 88.72 behind Nico Collins' 30.8. Adam falls to 1-3 and the odds sheet already has him on upset alert.

Jackson's Ha Ha Ha, Now Heres A Guy stayed perfect, beating BedBathNBIJAN22 137.94 to 113.82 to join Trip at 4-0. John is 2-2 now and still sitting on 533.38 points for, more than some teams with winning records, which is its own kind of tragedy.
Only one game this week finished inside a single possession. Everything else was a crime scene. Fourteen teams, seven games, and about half of you should be asking your co-managers for a polygraph.
data.signOff: Set your lineups, 11 weeks left, and somebody check on Matt.

data.headline: Hog Tied, Deep Fried, And Served Last At The Table
data.deck: Bearcat's 73.02 is the lowest number in the building, and his team name basically wrote its own obituary.
body: Somewhere in a kitchen, something named Hog Tied and Deep Fried was marinating all week for this exact outcome, and Sunday it finally got basted in its own juices. Bearcat put up 73.02 against Josef's Zyn-bo Squisher, who strolled to 112.7 without even needing to sweat, and the margin landed at a tidy, humiliating 39.68. That is not a loss. That is a eulogy with a scoreboard attached.

Bearcat's record now sits at 1-3, pointsFor stuck at 411.76, good for seed 11 in a 14 team gutter he is fighting to climb out of. The power rankings actually bumped him up a single spot to rank 10 this week, which is the fantasy football equivalent of getting promoted to assistant manager at the restaurant that just failed its health inspection. The playoff odds have him at 25.5 percent with the tag In Trouble, which honestly feels generous after a performance that makes 'in trouble' sound like a vacation.

The worst part is there is no excuse to hide behind. No name on this roster shows up anywhere near the top performers list this week. Nobody on Hog Tied and Deep Fried did anything. Not a quiet fine week, not a near miss, just a full team shutdown while Tetairoa McMillan was out there going for 45.2 for somebody else's fantasy and Bearcat's lineup sat there like it forgot football was being played on Sunday. 73.02 points across an entire roster is the kind of number you get benching your actual players and starting the concept of effort instead.

This is the inaugural Shart for Bearcat this season, which means he is a rookie in the one category nobody wants veteran experience in. Congratulations, sir. You earned this one clean, no asterisks, no bad beat, just a genuinely putrid Sunday that the league will not let you forget. 11 more weeks remain, which is 11 more chances to never see this number again.

So here it is, the full horrifying tribute. Forget the pitchers, forget the glasses, go straight to the hose in the backyard, the one with the kink in it that always sprays sideways, and drink from it anyway while kneeling in the exact spot of your driveway where Hog Tied and Deep Fried died at 73.02. Do it slow. Do it proud. Chug, bitch.
data.signOff: So here it is, the full horrifying tribute. Forget the pitchers, forget the glasses, go straight to the hose in the backyard, the one with the kink in it that always sprays sideways, and drink from it anyway while kneeling in the exact spot of your driveway where Hog Tied and Deep Fried died at 73.02. Do it slow. Do it proud. Chug, bitch.

data.headline: Taylor Chases Zero While Trip And Jackson Chase Perfection
data.deck: Week 4 sets up a two horse race at the top and a race to the bottom that smells exactly like the Shart Bowl should.
body: Two unbeaten teams, zero humility. Trip sits at 4-0 with 533.72 points for and gets Jackson Off on the road, a Ben squad stuck at 2-2 and clinging to a 50.1 playoff number. Trip is the favorite here by every measure that matters, and Ben knows it.

Across the league, Jackson is also 4-0 and welcomes Romo911 into his building. Aaron is 2-2 and riding a two time Shart Award resume that does not inspire confidence against the league's other perfect team. Jackson has lost zero fear and zero games, which is an ugly combination if you are Aaron.

The bubble has a real fight too. Jeff's Chase Browns with Downs, 76.7 percent to make the playoffs, travels to face John's BedBathNBIJAN22, sitting right behind him at 77 percent. One of these guys is about to feel a lot better about November.

Now the part you came for. Victorious Secrets has scored 347.1 points for the entire season, dead last in the league by a mile, and Taylor is 0-4 heading into a date with Josef's 3-1 Zyn-bo Squisher. Taylor has not found an offense yet this year and there is no reason to think it shows up now. Circle it. Shart Bowl.

data.headline: Taylor Got a 36.7 and Still Got Smoked
data.deck: The week's biggest individual numbers, including one that got buried alive in a 45.62 point massacre
body: Tetairoa McMillan went off for 45.2 and somehow that is not even the saddest story in this section. Jack rode him to a 154.78 demolition of Bibi's Ballers 69, which is what you're supposed to do when a rookie decides he's Moss for a day.

CeeDee Lamb dropped 41.3 on Sean's roster in the nail biter of the week, a 2.84 point classic that Sean somehow survived. Lamb basically carried Burrowed Alive on his back and the margin still came down to spare change.

Now the horror show. Kyren Williams went for 36.7, an absolute monster line, and it belonged to Taylor. Victorious Secrets still lost by 45.62. Taylor got the best fantasy performance on his roster all season and the final was 78.86. That's not bad luck, that's a crime scene.
Javonte Williams put up 31.3 for Jeff, Kenneth Walker gave Trip 30.9, and Nico Collins got Aaron to 30.8. All three of those guys won. Taylor did not. Let that sink in.

data.headline: The Hardware: Week 4 Awards Ceremony
data.deck: No trophies in the case, just men in a group chat judging each other with numbers. Let's hand out the hardware nobody asked for.
body: Pull up a folding chair and pretend this means something, because tonight we are doing the honors. No engraving, no plaque, just vibes and a spreadsheet. Let's get into it.

The Eyesore Award goes to Taylor and Victorious Secrets, who mustered 78.86 and lost by 45.62 to Trip's 50 Shades of Zay. Kyren Williams went off for 36.7 on Taylor's own roster and it still wasn't close to enough, which is almost impressive in a sad, clinical way.

The Juggernaut Award belongs to Jack and Cook'd, who dropped 154.78 on Bibi's Ballers 69 and didn't sweat a drop of it. Tetairoa McMillan put up 45.2 points by himself, which is the kind of stat line that makes other owners quietly check their waiver wire at 2 a.m.

The Razor's Edge Award is Sean's. Burrowed Alive squeaked past Jackson Off 149.42 to 146.58, a 2.84 margin that probably took ten years off both of their lives. CeeDee Lamb's 41.3 for Sean was the difference between a trophy and a eulogy.

The Mercy Rule Award also lands on Trip's desk, since 50 Shades of Zay's 45.62 margin over Victorious Secrets was less a football game and more a public service announcement about roster construction.

The Human Highlight Reel goes to Tetairoa McMillan one more time, 45.2 points, the single biggest number anybody produced this week. Everyone else on every other roster combined just got outworked by one Panther.
And finally, The Shart. We already dragged him through the mud in the lead story, so we'll just tip the cap here: Taylor's 78.86 speaks for itself. Go read it again if you need to feel worse.

data.headline: Jack Drops 154.78 and Still Can't Escape the Bubble
data.deck: Cook'd puts up the week's biggest number against the league's worst product and somehow still shows up tagged Bubble on Thursday.
body: Jack's Cook'd squad dropped 154.78 on Bibi's Ballers 69 this week, the top score in all of Squirtnite FFL, and he did it riding Tetairoa McMillan who went off for 45.2 points. That is not a floor game. That is a ceiling game. That is a man who set his lineup on Sunday morning, watched McMillan torch Carolina's secondary all afternoon, and got to spend the rest of the day feeling like the smartest guy in a 14-team league.
Credit where it's due. 154.78 is 154.78 no matter who you hang it on.

Now the undercut. Andrew's Bibi's Ballers 69 came in sitting at 1-3 and left down 44.02, which means Jack's big beautiful number landed on the single softest target available this week. A gentleman's blowout against a team already circling the drain. The margin tells you everything about how competitive this actually was, which is to say not very.

And here's the real kicker. Jack sits 3-1, fifth seed, and his playoff odds still read 48.4 percent with a Bubble tag next to his name. You can put up the league's best score of the week and the algorithm still looks at you like a guy it's not sure about. Cook'd next week against Shough Her Gently should be an easy one on paper, but so was this week, and the odds still don't believe in you, Jack. Prove them wrong or don't. Either way the scoreboard already liked you more than the standings do.
data.signOff: Keep stacking the ceiling games, Jack. The bubble's gonna need more than one big Sunday to pop.

data.headline: The Trade Desk Is A Crime Scene And Nobody Called It In
data.deck: Zero trades processed in Week 4. Grading an empty inbox is hard, but I found a way to be mad about it anyway.
body: Let's get the official business out of the way: there were no trades this week. None. The desk is empty. I sat here with my grading pen ready to hand out an F to somebody's cousin's keeper-league special and instead I got silence, which honestly might be the most damning grade of all.

Look at this league. Taylor is 0-4 and sitting on 347.1 points for, dead last, Victorious Secrets in name only. Matt's Shough Her Gently just got run over 115.9 to 87.38 and still didn't pick up the phone. Sean's Burrowed Alive squeaked out a 149.42 to 146.58 win over Ben and is still 1-3 on the season, somehow both hot and homeless. These are exactly the circumstances where a man is supposed to panic-trade his bench into oblivion, and instead everybody just sat on their hands like it's a closed casket.

Meanwhile Trip and Jackson are both 4-0, Aaron's Romo911 has shart counts piling up like parking tickets, and not one desperate GM thought to try to pry something loose. Grade for the week: incomplete, across the board, for cowardice. Make a move, gentlemen. The byes are coming and your rosters are not going to fix themselves.
data.signOff: Pick up the phone next week. I'm begging you.
